question: Which SO(4), hence analytically continued Lorentz, pieces of the completed 10 and 14 irreps are already present in the original candidate48 scalar ansatz?
conclusion: The original 102-field ansatz directly seeds two distinct four-vector sectors in the active-active block.
Neither the Lorentz bivector6 nor the metric-like symmetric-traceless9 is present directly.
The bivector, scalar, and rank-two sectors arise only after completing the SO(5) orbit; after real-form continuation they are symmetry descendants of the seeded vectors.
researchDirection: Treat the generated rank-two9 as an emergent response descendant and test whether its quadratic dynamics is induced consistently from the vector seed, rather than calling it a fundamental metric field.
falsifier: The indirect-only conclusion fails if an independent projector finds seed rank above zero or projection energy above 1e-10 in the bivector6, scalar1, or rank-two9 sectors.
nextBranches: Compute explicit odd-generator maps from each seeded vector4 into the scalar1, bivector6, and rank-two9 descendants.
Measure whether the generated rank-two quadratic form has the Fierz-Pauli trace constraint.
Test if the two seeded vector4 sectors are coupled or orthogonal under the candidate48 Hessian.
